description: Pair entries, theme lines and feeling links drafted on 16 October 2026 so every combination of blocks gets feedback. Not reviewed; no example games, since none were checked. The curated entries in interactions.json come first.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move around the board, and the spaces you land on let you pick from a shared row of cards.
pros: The dice decide where you go, the cards give you a choice.
Easy to start, with something to think about each turn.
cons: A low roll can leave only poor cards to pick from.
Picking can slow down a game that feels quick.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and some spaces start an auction where everyone offers to pay for a prize.
pros: Auctions give everyone a reason to pay attention on other turns.
Money matters, not only lucky rolls.
cons: Landing on auction spaces is still down to the dice.
Players who are low on money can feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: You keep rolling to move further, but one unlucky roll can send you back.
pros: Every roll is a little gamble you choose to take.
cons: A long run of unlucky rolls can feel unfair.
Careful players may move very slowly.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move pieces around a board and try to hold spaces before others reach them.
pros: Big moments when a roll lands you right where you need.
The board changes as people take ground.
cons: The dice can decide who gets the key spaces.
Players far behind can find it hard to catch up.

pairs.tendency: Dice decide how far you move or how many workers you get, then you place them on actions.
pros: Mixes luck and planning in one turn.
Every turn offers a few real options.
cons: A poor roll can block your plan.
Two systems to learn at once can feel heavy.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and where you land gives you pieces to build a shape or pattern.
pros: Puzzle-building with a bit of surprise.
cons: You might not land where the piece you need is.
Players can end up waiting for one lucky space.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and cards in your hand let you change the roll or do something extra.
pros: Cards give you some control over the dice.
Saving a card for the right moment feels clever.
cons: Tracking cards and dice together takes some care.
A hand of weak cards does not help much.

pairs.tendency: Players win card tricks, and each trick won lets them move forward on a track.
pros: Every hand of cards pushes the race on.
Card skill turns into movement you can see.
cons: The movement part can feel like an extra step.
One player who wins many tricks can run away.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and you can make deals with others to swap spaces, money or favours.
pros: Talking and dealing make every turn social.
Clever deals can make up for poor rolls.
cons: Long talks can slow the game down.
Quieter players can get left out of deals.

pairs.tendency: You roll around the board, and each space gives you a card towards a matching set.
pros: Simple to learn, with a clear goal.
Each roll can bring the piece you need.
cons: Finishing a set can depend on luck.
Players can collect without ever meeting each other.

pairs.tendency: You roll to see which tile you take or how far you go, then place tiles to grow the board.
pros: The map grows differently every game.
Placing tiles gives you something to plan.
cons: The dice can hand you tiles that do not fit.
Moving and placing can make turns long.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the right to pick first, then choose cards from a shared set.
pros: Going first costs something, so every choice matters.
Lots of small decisions each round.
cons: Two steps every round can slow things down.
Players short on money pick last again and again.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing cards to pick from, but if you draw one too many you lose the round.
pros: Picking feels tense because you might stop too late.
Every draw is a small risk.
cons: Stopping too late can wipe out a whole round.
Players who never take risks can fall behind.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that let them place pieces on a map to hold areas.
pros: The cards you pick shape the map.
Watching what others pick tells you what they want.
cons: Taking a card just to block someone can feel mean.
The game can get crowded and slow.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards that give you more workers or new action spaces to use.
pros: Your choices build up how strong your turns are.
Lots of ways to plan ahead.
cons: Many options can freeze younger players.
Early picks can decide too much.

pairs.tendency: You pick tiles or cards from a shared pool and fit them into your own pattern.
pros: Taking a piece someone else needs is a quiet move.
cons: Looking at everyone's pattern takes time.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards into your hand, then choose when to play them.
pros: Picking and saving cards gives a lot of control.
Planning a few turns ahead pays off.
cons: Many cards to think about at once.
New players can find it slow.

pairs.tendency: Players pick their hand from a shared pile before playing tricks with it.
pros: You get some say over the cards you play with.
Knowing what others took helps you guess their tricks.
cons: The picking part adds time to each hand.
Experienced players can plan far ahead of new ones.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards and can trade or promise them to each other.
pros: Lots of talking about who takes what.
Deals can change what everyone picks.
cons: Promises can be broken, which may upset some players.
Talks can make picking very slow.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards from a shared row to build matching sets, watching what others collect.
pros: Every pick moves your sets forward.
Taking a card someone needs is a quiet move.
cons: The card you need may be taken first.

pairs.tendency: You pick tiles from a shared offer and place them to build the board.
pros: The board grows from everyone's picks.
Each pick is a little puzzle.
cons: Taking tiles just to block others is easy and can feel unkind.
The offer can run out of tiles you need.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on rewards, and the winner then risks pushing for more or stopping safely.
pros: Big moments when someone wins a bid and goes for more.
Paying more means taking a bigger risk.
cons: Losing a costly bid and then busting can sting.
Cautious players may never win anything big.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the right to place pieces or take control of areas.
pros: Every area has a price you decide.
Spending carefully is part of the plan.
cons: Players short on money can lose all the main areas.
Bidding over and over can feel slow.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the top action spaces before placing their workers.
pros: The top spots cost more, so everyone thinks about value.
No one gets the top action for free.
cons: Two steps each round can drag.
Rich players keep getting the top spots.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on pieces and then fit the pieces they win into their own pattern.
pros: You decide how much a piece is worth to you.
Puzzles stay personal even when bids are shared.
cons: Losing a piece you needed can break a pattern.
Bidding wars can take a while.

pairs.tendency: Players use cards from their hand as bids, so every bid uses up a card.
pros: Spending cards wisely is the whole game.
Saving strong cards for later feels clever.
cons: One wasted card can hurt for a long time.
Planning the whole hand takes focus.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on how many tricks they will win, then try to win exactly that many.
pros: Guessing your own hand makes every trick matter.
cons: Being one trick off can feel harsh.
It takes a few rounds to understand.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on prizes and can make deals to stop bidding against each other.
pros: Deals and promises shape every auction.
cons: Quieter players can be left out.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on cards and collect them into matching sets.
pros: You know exactly why each card matters to you.
Watching what others collect changes your bids.
cons: Paying too much for one card can ruin a set.
Bidding for every card takes time.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on tiles and place the ones they win to build the board.
pros: The board grows from what people chose to pay for.
Each tile has a different value to each player.
cons: Losing bids can leave you with nothing to place.
Many rounds of bidding can slow the game.

pairs.tendency: You keep pushing to take more areas, but stretching too far can lose them all.
pros: Big swings when someone takes a risk and it works.
cons: One failed push can knock you out of the running.
Careful players can feel left behind.

pairs.tendency: You can place extra workers on risky spaces that might pay off or might lose them.
pros: Risky spots give everyone a tempting choice.
Safe and risky plans can both work.
cons: Losing workers can leave you with little to do.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing pieces to finish a pattern, but one wrong piece can spoil it.
pros: Every draw feels exciting near the end of a pattern.
Stopping early is a real choice.
cons: A spoiled pattern can feel like wasted work.
Some players stop too early to enjoy it.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing cards into your hand, but going over a limit loses them.
pros: Deciding when to stop is the main thrill.
Cards you keep can help later.
cons: Busting loses a whole round of work.
Players who never risk can be slow.

pairs.tendency: Players can bid to win more tricks than is safe, earning more if they make it.
pros: Bold calls make every hand exciting.
Getting exactly what you called feels clever.
cons: Players who always play safe can fall behind.

pairs.tendency: Players can make risky deals, promising more than they are sure they can give.
pros: Lots of bold promises and laughter.
cons: Players who avoid deals can miss out.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing cards to finish a set, but a wrong card can make you lose what you drew.
pros: Every draw could finish your set.
Stopping safely is always an option.
cons: Losing a nearly complete set stings.
Luck can matter more than planning.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing tiles to place, but one that does not fit can end your turn.
pros: The board grows in sudden bursts.
Tense moments with each new tile.
cons: Turns can end with nothing placed.
Long lucky turns can leave others waiting.

pairs.tendency: Placing workers on action spaces lets you send pieces to hold areas on the map.
pros: Two kinds of competition: for actions and for land.
Planning both at once feels deep.
cons: A lot to keep track of.
Losing the key action can cost you an area.

pairs.tendency: Players hold areas on a board that score more when they form a shape or pattern.
pros: Thinking about shapes makes the map more interesting.
Blocking someone's pattern is a clear move.
cons: Reading the whole board can be slow.
One broken pattern can be hard to recover from.

pairs.tendency: Cards in your hand let you move or place pieces to take areas.
pros: Playing the right card at the right time feels clever.
Saving cards for a big move is a real plan.
cons: A poor hand can leave you unable to fight back.
Many cards and pieces to manage.

pairs.tendency: Winning a trick lets you take or hold an area on the map.
pros: Each trick has something you can see on the board.
Card play and the map connect.
cons: The map can feel like an extra layer to track.
Strong hands can win many areas at once.

pairs.tendency: Players make deals about who gets which areas, and can break them.
pros: Lots of talking, alliances and surprises.
Peace deals and betrayals keep the game lively.
cons: Broken deals can lead to real arguments.
Quieter players can be pushed out.

pairs.tendency: Holding areas gives you cards or pieces towards a matching set.
pros: The map and the sets support each other.
Choosing which area to take is a real decision.
cons: Losing an area can break a set.
Two goals at once can confuse new players.

pairs.tendency: Players place tiles to build the map and put pieces on them to claim areas.
pros: The board you fight over is one you built together.
Placing a tile can open or close an area.
cons: Busy boards can be hard to read.
Early tiles can decide a lot.

pairs.tendency: Placing workers gets you pieces to fit into your own pattern or shape.
pros: Planning which pieces you need is satisfying.
cons: Someone taking your action can break your plan.

pairs.tendency: Cards in your hand change what your workers can do on action spaces.
pros: More ways to plan each turn.
Cards let you make surprise moves.
cons: Hard for new players to see what to do.

pairs.tendency: Winning tricks earns you workers or the first pick of action spaces.
pros: Card play feeds your plans on the board.
cons: Two different games to learn at once.
A run of weak cards can leave you with few workers.

pairs.tendency: Players can make deals to let each other use blocked action spaces.
pros: Deals open up actions that seemed closed.
Talking is part of every round.
cons: Deals can take a long time.
Players who do not deal can feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: Placing workers gets you items to collect into matching sets.
pros: Watching others' sets helps you block them.
cons: Losing the action you need can stall a set.

pairs.tendency: Workers collect tiles, and you place the tiles to build your area or a shared board.
pros: Your board grows from your choices.
cons: Early mistakes can be hard to fix.

pairs.tendency: You choose which cards from your hand to use to complete a pattern.
pros: Deciding what to keep and what to play feels thoughtful.
cons: A hand without the right cards can stall you.

pairs.tendency: Tricks you win give you cards to fit into a pattern.
pros: Winning tricks feeds a bigger puzzle.
Choosing which trick to win is a real decision.
cons: Two things to think about each hand.
Losing tricks can leave patterns unfinished.

pairs.tendency: Players trade pieces with each other to finish their own patterns.
pros: Trading gives everyone a reason to talk.
Helping someone can help you too.
cons: Players can refuse to trade and stall others.

pairs.tendency: You collect matching items and arrange them in a pattern for extra points.
pros: Two kinds of matching in one game.
cons: Rules for scoring can get complicated.

pairs.tendency: You place tiles to form shapes or patterns that score points.
pros: Each tile is a little puzzle.
cons: Running out of space can end your plans.
Players can go quiet while thinking.

pairs.tendency: You plan which cards to keep and when to play them across a hand of tricks.
pros: Playing the right card at the right time feels clever.
cons: Takes a few games to learn well.

pairs.tendency: Players trade cards from their hands and make deals about what to play.
pros: Clever trades can turn a weak hand around.
cons: People may hold back cards others need.

pairs.tendency: You hold cards in your hand and choose when to play them into sets.
pros: Waiting to play a full set feels tense.
cons: Holding too many cards can cost you.
A hand that never matches can be frustrating.

pairs.tendency: Cards in your hand show which tiles you can place and where.
pros: Planning where tiles go feels thoughtful.
Each card gives a few choices.
cons: A poor hand can leave few useful moves.

pairs.tendency: Players can talk and make deals about which tricks they will try to win.
pros: Talking adds a social layer to card play.
Deals can help a weak hand.

pairs.tendency: Cards you win in tricks go into sets that score points.
pros: Every trick could finish a set.
Choosing which trick to win matters.
cons: Your hand may not let you win what you need.
Scoring at the end can take a while.

pairs.tendency: Winning a trick lets you place a tile on the board.
pros: Card play builds something you can see.
Each trick has a clear reward.
cons: Strong hands can control the board.

pairs.tendency: Players trade cards to finish their own matching sets.
pros: Helping others can help you too.
cons: Some players may refuse to trade.

pairs.tendency: Players make deals about where tiles go on a shared board.
pros: Deals shape how the map grows.
cons: Decisions can take a long time.

pairs.tendency: You collect tiles and place them in matching groups to score.
cons: You may not get the tile you need.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move around the board and collect points from the spaces you land on.
pros: Simple to learn and quick to play.
cons: Luck can decide who scores most.
Players can feel they have few choices.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and landing on some spaces knocks players out until one is left.
pros: Every roll can change the game.
cons: Players knocked out early have to wait.
Luck can knock out a careful player.

pairs.tendency: Everyone rolls to move together, trying to reach safety before the danger catches up.
pros: Easy for groups to play together.
cons: Unlucky rolls can sink the whole team.

pairs.tendency: Players roll to move as a team towards one shared goal on the board.
cons: The dice decide most of the game.
Some players can feel they did nothing.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, each player secretly trying to reach their own places on the board.
pros: Guessing what others are after adds mystery.
Your path matters to you alone.
cons: Dice can stop you reaching your goal.
Others may never notice what you were doing.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move along a story path, and the game ends when the story is told.
pros: The board feels like a journey.
cons: Rolls can feel like they do not matter to the story.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that move them forward, racing to be first to the end.
pros: Each pick is a step in the race.
Taking a card someone needs slows them down.
cons: Early picks can decide who wins.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that attack or protect, until only one player is left.
pros: Every pick is about staying in.
Choosing between attack and defence is a real decision.
cons: Players knocked out early have to wait.
Ganging up on one player can happen.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards together to fight off a danger that threatens everyone.
pros: Choosing cards as a team means lots of talking.
cons: One player can end up deciding for everyone.
A weak set of cards can doom the team.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards to help the group reach one shared goal.
pros: Picking for the team feels generous.
cons: Some players can feel their picks did not matter.
Strong players may tell others what to pick.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards, each secretly working towards their own goal.
pros: Guessing why someone took a card is fun.
Taking a card can quietly block someone.
cons: Your goal may need cards others take first.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that add scenes to a story, and the game ends when the story is complete.
pros: Picks shape where the story goes.
cons: Choosing for the story and for yourself can clash.

pairs.tendency: Players bid to move forward, racing to the finish line.
pros: Spending money to move fast is a real choice.
cons: Players who spend early can run out.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on prizes worth points, and the most points at the end wins.
pros: Watching others' bids helps you plan.
cons: Overpaying once can cost you the game.
Lots of maths for some players.

pairs.tendency: Players bid to attack or defend, and anyone who runs out is knocked out.
pros: Tense bidding when someone is close to out.
cons: Players out early have to wait.
Rich players can push others out.

pairs.tendency: Players pool or bid resources together to hold off a danger.
cons: Arguments about who pays can start.
Running out of money can doom the team.

pairs.tendency: Players bid to decide who takes on which part of a shared goal.
cons: Some players may never win a bid.
Bidding can slow down a team game.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on items, each secretly wanting different things.
pros: Bids give hints about secret goals.
cons: Your goal may cost more than you can pay.
Hard to read for new players.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on story parts, and the story finishes when all parts are taken.
pros: Deciding what a story piece is worth is unusual and fun.
The story grows from everyone's bids.
cons: Bids can matter more than the story.

pairs.tendency: You keep taking risks to grab more points, but going too far loses them.
pros: Every turn has a big choice.
cons: Lucky players can run away with it.

pairs.tendency: Players take risks to stay in, and those who push too far are knocked out.
pros: Easy to follow who is still in.
cons: Players out early have to wait.
Luck can knock out a careful player.

pairs.tendency: The team decides together how far to push towards a shared goal before stopping.
pros: Group choices about risk lead to lively talk.
cons: One cautious or reckless voice can take over.

pairs.tendency: You take risks to reach your own secret goal without others seeing what you need.
pros: Risky moves can reveal your goal.
cons: Others may not notice your risks.

pairs.tendency: Players push their luck to move the story forward, risking setbacks.
pros: Every risk adds a twist to the story.
cons: Setbacks can make the story stall.

pairs.tendency: Players race to take a set number of areas first.
pros: A clear target keeps everyone focused.
Blocking someone near the finish is tense.
cons: Early leaders can be hard to stop.
Turns can be about blocking more than building.

pairs.tendency: Holding areas scores points, and the most points at the end wins.
pros: Every area has a clear value.
The board shows who is ahead.
cons: Scoring at the end can take a while.
Players far behind can lose interest.

pairs.tendency: Players work together to hold areas against a spreading danger.
pros: Defending the map as a team feels exciting.
cons: Losing one area can lead to losing many.

pairs.tendency: Players work together to take control of a set of areas.
pros: Planning who goes where leads to lots of talk.
cons: Some players may follow orders without thinking.

pairs.tendency: Players fight over areas, each secretly needing certain ones.
pros: Guessing why someone wants an area is fun.
Bluffing about where you are heading.
cons: Your areas may be taken by chance.
Secret goals can make fights confusing.

pairs.tendency: Holding areas moves a story forward, and the game ends when the story is done.
pros: Every area matters to the plot.
cons: Story and map can pull in different directions.

pros: Blocking someone's action can slow them.
cons: One player can pull ahead early.

cons: Players out early have to wait.

pairs.tendency: Players place workers together to keep everyone safe from a growing danger.

pairs.tendency: Players place workers together to build towards one shared goal.
cons: Some may feel their turns did not matter.

pros: Placements give hints about secret goals.
cons: Hard to tell who is ahead.

pairs.tendency: Workers carry out actions that move a story forward to its ending.
cons: The story can feel like extra rules.
The ending can arrive before you are ready.

pairs.tendency: Players race to be the first to complete their pattern.
cons: Luck in pieces can decide the race.

pairs.tendency: Patterns you complete score points, and the most points wins.
pros: Satisfying when a pattern comes together.

pairs.tendency: Players who cannot complete their pattern in time are knocked out, until one is left.
cons: Can feel harsh for slower thinkers.

cons: A missing piece can doom the team.

pairs.tendency: The whole group builds one big pattern together.
cons: Some may feel their piece was small.

cons: Hard to tell who is winning.

pairs.tendency: Completing patterns unlocks parts of a story.
cons: The story can feel stuck if a pattern stalls.

pros: Saving a big card for the final push feels clever.
cons: A weak hand can leave you behind.

pairs.tendency: Players choose when to play cards for points, and the most points wins.
cons: Holding cards too long can cost you.

pairs.tendency: Players use cards to stay in the game, and those with no useful cards are knocked out.
pros: Saving defensive cards is a real plan.
cons: A weak hand can feel hopeless.

pairs.tendency: Players use cards together to fight off a danger.
cons: Hands without the right cards can doom the team.

pairs.tendency: Players play cards towards one goal they share.
cons: Some players may feel their cards did not matter.

pros: Cards you keep hint at your goal.
cons: Your goal may need cards you never draw.

pros: Choosing which card to play shapes the story.

pairs.tendency: Tricks you win move you forward, racing to the end of a track.

themes.line: The abstract theme gives the game no story or setting, just shapes, colours and moves, so the rules are the whole experience.
The historical theme sets the game in a real time and place from the past, so the moves can stand for real events.
The fantasy theme brings dragons, magic or quests, so the same moves can feel like an adventure.
The science-fiction theme sets the game in space or the future, so the same moves can feel like exploring or inventing.
The everyday-life theme uses places players already know, like a market or a school, so the rules are easier to picture.
The absurd theme makes the setting silly on purpose, so players can laugh at their own moves.
The educational theme ties the game to something to learn, so playing also teaches a fact or a skill.
The real-world-issue theme connects the game to a problem people face today, so the moves can start a conversation.
The poetic theme makes the game short and a little strange, so the moves ask players to notice something rather than to win it.
The ritual-or-sacred theme turns the board into a path towards something holy, so each move can feel like a step in a practice.
The mortality-and-loss theme ties the game to time running out or someone being lost, so the moves can carry weight beyond the table.
